answer: Burned submission tickets put a fixed cost on every reward attempt. A verifier checks an irreversible burn receipt bound to the job, claimant and epoch, then consumes it once. Whether the job maps a knoll or classifies shale and copper, N attempts under N names need N separate burns. The attacker loses funds even on rejected work; set the fee above a junk attempt's expected reward. This requires no rebates or per-account bonuses. It prices spam rather than proving unique ownership; wealthy attackers can still pay.
